cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The course, path, or method by which something proceeds; in this text, the basic term for the Way being discussed.
cards.Nuance (English): Can also point to a way of doing or speaking, not only a physical path.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To express in words; to say or talk about.
cards.Nuance (English): Often takes the thing spoken about as its object or follows another verb-like use of the same form.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The Master speaks of the matter.|I do not dare to speak of it.|He too speaks of this meaning.|The people speak of it.
cards.Sentences: 子道其事。|吾不敢道之。|彼亦道此義。|眾人道焉。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical road, path, or route for travel.
cards.Nuance (English): A concrete spatial path, distinct from the abstract philosophical sense.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The cart travels on the road.|The gentleman follows the old road.|He is lost on the road.|The traveler asks for the way.
cards.Sentences: 車行其道。|士循舊道。|迷於道中。|行客問道。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates ability, possibility, or permission for an action to occur.
cards.Nuance (English): In this text it marks what is possible or admissible rather than moral approval.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates permission or allowance for something to be done.
cards.Nuance (English): Focuses on what is allowed rather than what is merely possible.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): One may enter this gate.|This matter may be permitted.|The people may go.|The saying may be accepted.
cards.Sentences: 可入此門。|此事可許。|眾人可往。|言可採也。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Fit to be accepted, approved, or regarded as proper.
cards.Nuance (English): Describes suitability or acceptability, not physical ability.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): His proposal is acceptable.|This method is acceptable.|Few words are acceptable when spoken.|The Way may be carried out.
cards.Sentences: 其議可。|此法可。|言而可者少。|道可行也。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negator marking denial or contradiction of the following predicate or statement.
cards.Nuance (English): Simple sentential negation here, not a noun or adjectival 'wrong' sense.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not right, improper, or in error; contrary to what is fitting or true.
cards.Nuance (English): Judges a thing as erroneous or improper rather than merely denying it.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): What he says is wrong.|Between right and wrong.|This intention is truly wrong.|Do not act contrary to ritual.
cards.Sentences: 其言非也。|是非之間。|此意實非。|非禮勿動。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A way or course that is enduring and unchanging; the stable normative Way.
cards.Nuance (English): Combines permanence with the sense of the Way as a guiding principle, not a merely ordinary habit.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A word or designation used to identify or describe something.
cards.Nuance (English): Can be contrasted with the actual reality or thing named, as in discussions of naming and naming limits.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give a designation to something or to mention it by name.
cards.Nuance (English): A verbal use that can take an object directly or in a naming construction.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The father names his son.|The people name the mountain.|I do not dare to name it.|The king names this thing.
cards.Sentences: 子名其子。|眾人名山。|不敢名之。|王名此物。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed or enduring designation, as opposed to a changeable one.
cards.Nuance (English): Emphasizes permanence in naming, not simply an ordinary name.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
cards.Sentences: S道可道，非常道，名可名，非常名；

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks the absence or nonexistence of what follows; also forms negative predicative constructions.
cards.Nuance (English): In the Laozi it often opposes 有 and points to absence as a condition or principle.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Without name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used before a noun to mean there is none or none of the thing in question.
cards.Nuance (English): Negates the existence or presence of the noun it modifies.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): No one has arrived.|There is nothing to say.|Travel without a cart.|A thing without a name.
cards.Sentences: 無人至。|無事可言。|無車而行。|無名之物。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): Nonbeing, absence, or the state of there being nothing.
cards.Nuance (English): Treats absence itself as a substantive notion.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Nonbeing arises from being.|Change arises from nothing.|Hold to emptiness.|Know its absence.
cards.Sentences: 無生於有。|無中生變。|守其無。|知其無也。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The totality of the cosmos, often used as a pair for the whole natural world.
cards.Nuance (English): A paired cosmic expression, not simply two separate nouns in this usage.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Without name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A genitive or attributive particle linking one noun to another, marking possession, relation, or modification.
cards.Nuance (English): Here it links a noun to the head noun that follows, without carrying independent lexical content.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Without name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person pronoun referring to a previously mentioned or contextually understood person or thing.
cards.Nuance (English): Often used as an object pronoun or after certain verbs and prepositions.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): See him/it.|Love him/it.|Abandon him/it.|Follow him/it.
cards.Sentences: 見之。|愛之。|棄之。|從之。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move toward or depart for a place.
cards.Nuance (English): A directional verb, not a genitive particle.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): I go east.|The gentleman goes to the city.|The man goes to the market.|The horse goes to the plain.
cards.Sentences: 吾之東。|士之城。|人之市。|馬之野。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): The initial point, origin, or first stage of something.
cards.Nuance (English): Highlights the first point in a sequence or the origin of a process.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Without name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
cards.Sentences: S無名，天地之始，有名，萬物之母。

cards.Dictionary Meaning (English): To start an action, process, or state.
cards.Nuance (English): A dynamic verbal use of the same form, not the noun 'beginning'.
cards.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi recension
cards.Sentence Translations (English): Now one begins to learn.|The teacher begins to speak.|The matter begins now.|The people begin to be at peace.
cards.Sentences: 今始學。|師始言。|事始於今。|民始安。
